title: Weather and Time Descriptions in the Imperfecto

sections.content: Weather, time expressions, and atmospheric descriptions are always in the imperfecto — they are ongoing background conditions, not completed events.

items.spanish: Llovía mucho cuando salí de casa.
items.english: It was raining a lot when I left the house.

items.spanish: Eran las dos de la mañana cuando sonó el teléfono.
items.english: It was two in the morning when the phone rang.

items.spanish: Hacía un calor terrible pero decidimos salir de todas formas.
items.english: It was terribly hot but we decided to go out anyway.

items.spanish: El cielo estaba completamente despejado cuando empezó la tormenta.
items.english: The sky was completely clear when the storm began.

sections.content: Weather verbs in imperfecto: llovía (it was raining), nevaba (it was snowing), hacía calor/frío/viento/sol, había niebla/nubes. These always describe the background, never a completed event.
